Another outing at the Fukuoka Marathon, however, saw him enter as favourite but drop out at 32 km. hop_3.question: Who set the second world record in the history of the Fukuoka Marathon?
hop_3.doc:
"Fukuoka Marathon"
had three straight wins in 1971 to 1973 and a fourth win came in 1974, the same year that the race took on its current title of the . In 1980, Toshihiko Seko won in a time of 2:09:45 hours, just four seconds ahead of Takeshi So. This represented the first time that two men had completed the marathon distance under two hours and ten minutes at the same competition. hop_4.question: Who is Robert de Castella's brother?
hop_4.doc:
"Robert de Castella"
took part in four World Cross Country Championships, whereas brother Anthony competed in running at club level for more than 25 years. Rob de Castella was an outstanding track athlete as a teenager and trained under Pat Clohessy from the age of 11. De Castella first came to international attention when he won the 1981 Fukuoka Marathon in a time of 2:08:18, which was the fastest time recorded for an out-and-back course.
